item: Comfort — the person in crisis (comfort path)
angle: Design the whole comfort experience: the path, and the one-tap comfort every other path needs, with the safety and the human being at the end of it.
thesis: Comfort is not a path someone picks on a good day — it is a moment they fall into, usually late, usually alone, usually from whatever screen they were already on. So comfort has to be reachable in one tap from every path without changing anyone's saved path, has to hand over the deliverable (one verse, one chapter, read aloud) before it asks for a single thing, and has to put a real person and a region-correct crisis line on the same screen as the scripture, not two taps away in More. Ashley's instinct here is already right and the research confirms it: just the scriptures, nothing asked, no graduation. What the research adds is duty of care (only 35% of mental-health apps show crisis resources in-app; some show the wrong country's number) and what the code review adds is that the screen currently shows today's chapter twice and asks a person in crisis to commit to a daily reading amount — which breaks the path's own printed promise, "Comfort scriptures. Nothing else asked of you."
principles: The deliverable is at the top and already open. The verse, then Listen, then the chapter — never a Read button hiding the thing they came for.
Nothing is asked. Not an amount, not an email, not a notification, not a path change, not a rating. Anything the app can infer, it infers silently.
Nothing counts. No streak shown, no 'Reading 2 of 3', no 'complete', no grading ('You're doing great'). The streak keeps recording for Ashley's numbers and stays invisible.
The crisis line and the pastor are on the reading screen, always, offline included — never behind a tab, never behind a network call.
A safety card never blocks, never lectures, never reports. It appears beside the answer and the answer still comes.
Comfort never nudges. No push, no 'we missed you', no seasonal challenge, no graduation to another path — ever.
One passage. Low stimulus. If two things on the screen are both scripture, one of them is noise.

journey.day0: Two arrivals, both one tap. (a) The path card already in the sheet — 'I'm going through something hard / Comfort scriptures. Nothing else asked of you' (i18n.ts:935-937) — saves the path and opens the screen (ChoosePathSheet commit ruling). (b) NEW: the comfort tap, from any other path, which opens the same screen full-screen and changes nothing — no saveSetup call at all, so no source is ever stamped (coldStart.ts:21 REAL_CHOICE_SOURCES rule). Either way: no PathAskedOnce (already exempt), no push ask (App.tsx:312 already exempt), no email gate, no streak. Research: 'Crisis is not a persona someone chooses on a good day.'
journey.first_session: Two to four minutes. Greeting with no day count. Today's anchor verse, large. Listen (audio first — the research's delivery note). The chapter open underneath, in the white paper hero panel. 'Pray this with me' if they want it, and it stays open until they close it. 'I've finished reading' brings one short thought from that chapter. Then 'That's enough for today.' Talk to someone is on screen the whole time, not revealed at the end.
journey.return_visit: Same shape, next chapter in the 30-day rotation, keyed to the local date. No reference to the gap, no count, no welcome-back. From day two, one quiet line above the verse: 'Still here. Want the same passage, or a new one?' — the one element in this design the research explicitly flags as plausible but unsourced, so it ships as an A/B, not as fact.
journey.week2: If they read more than one chapter on two separate days, the app quietly sets dw_comfort_daily to that amount and says so once in the done state ('There'll be two ready for you tomorrow') with a 'Change this' link. It never asks the question. If they made a steady card it now sits under the reading. Still no streak, no push, no graduation prompt, no 'Feeling Stronger?' (removed for good, locked by pathway-upgrades.test.ts:27).
journey.missed_day: Nothing happens. No 'we missed you', no reset message, no gap in a chart, no badge. recordStreakToday() still runs on mount and still pushes to cloud; the UI still suppresses it for comfort (HomeScreen.tsx:2004-2006). The screen on day nine looks exactly like the screen on day two. Research: guilt-framed reminders drive opt-out and uninstall.
journey.seasonal: Comfort opts out of the calendar. No Lent challenge, no 1 January plan start, no church-wide reading count — the research's calendar-spike finding is about the other four paths, and a time-boxed challenge aimed at someone in crisis is a demand. One exception for Ashley to rule on: the days the whole church is praying about a specific loss or disaster get one line above the verse, never a plan.

Amount inferred from behaviour: shows the inferred value, selected, with no explanation of how it got there.
Signed-in pastor on the comfort path: allowed, with the sign-out row beside it and no lock glyph.

comfort_access: Three doors, mirroring the pattern Ashley already ruled for the path sheet, and none of them a gate. (1) The path card in the one 'Where are you today?' sheet — 'I'm going through something hard' — which saves comfort as a real choice and opens it, unchanged. (2) NEW, the comfort tap: one quiet line under the reading on every other path's Home, 'Having a hard day? Open comfort', which opens the full-screen Comfort Now surface and never calls saveSetup, so the person's saved path, plan, streak and progress are untouched. (3) A row at the top of More, 'I need comfort today', reachable when they are not on Home. The prayer-request flow in Messages is a fourth, incidental route — the safety card there links straight into the same care card. What is deliberately not a door: a sixth card on the path sheet (it is five cards and must fit a phone without scrolling), a header icon competing with the PathSwatch, and any interstitial. Once inside, comfort is reachable again from the same three places every day, and the app never asks whether they want to stay.
reminders: None. Comfort gets no push notification, ever — App.tsx:312 already excludes the comfort persona from the push opt-in, and that stays. The research is direct about why: guilt-framed streak reminders drive notification opt-out and uninstall, and the harm list for this persona names guilt outright. So there is no reminder to design; the only 'return' mechanic is the in-app check-in on the next visit, which they have to open the app to see. Two consequences to state plainly. First, comfort will look worse than every other path on any retention metric that depends on a nudge — that is expected and must not be read as failure. Second, if someone arrives at comfort via the tap while their saved path is congregation or deeper_study, their own path's reminder keeps running unchanged; the tap must not touch push state in either direction. The one thing worth Ashley's ruling later: whether a person who has used the comfort tap three times in a week gets one message — and if so, it comes from a pastor, not from the app.
instrumentation: comfort_opened {source: path|tap|more|prayer, persona_at_open, first_time} — proves comfort-tap reach from the other four paths, which is the research's named test and the number that says whether door 2 was worth building.
comfort_listen_started / comfort_listen_completed {ref, seconds} — proves the audio-first delivery ordering; if listens are near zero, Listen is in the wrong place, not the wrong feature.

comfort_passage_read {ref, source} — fires when they tap 'I've finished reading'. Must NOT credit a plan day and must not route through handleRead; the arrival seed for comfort is credit-free by ruling.
comfort_prayer_opened {ref} — the guided prayer is the retained crisis-facing feature; this is the only evidence it earns its place.
comfort_care_tapped {channel: pastor|line, region, region_source} — the duty-of-care number. If pastor taps happen and nobody at that campus answers, that is a failure with a name on it.

comfort_line_shown {region, region_source: campus|ip|timezone|unknown} — watch the unknown rate. A high unknown rate means people in crisis are seeing no number, which is the exact industry failure the research names.

comfort_safety_shown {surface: ai|prayer, lang} and comfort_safety_dismissed {surface, seconds_to_dismiss} — trigger rate and a false-positive proxy. Fast dismissals clustering means the word list is too loose. The text that triggered it is never sent.
comfort_steady_saved {fields_filled: 1-3} and comfort_steady_opened — Wysa's equivalent was used by over 49% of crisis users; if ours is under 10%, the card is in the wrong place on the screen.

comfort_return_next_day {entry_source, days_since_last} — D1/D7/D30 for this path specifically. No public source exists for Bible-app retention or for comfort-to-discipleship transition; only our own instrumentation can ever answer it, and this path is the first place it matters.
comfort_daily_inferred {n} — proves the inference actually fires now that the question is gone. If this never fires, dw_comfort_daily silently stays 0 and the tomorrow line never appears.
comfort_offline_render {had_text: bool, had_line: bool} — proves the crisis number and the chapter really do render with no network. This is the one event that must never be zero-truthy.
self_serve_levers: Move the comfort content out of src/data/comfort.ts into public/comfort/content.json — 30 entries of {chapter, anchorVerseRef, anchorVerseText, devotion, prayer} in en/es/pt/id. A campus pastor edits a JSON file, not TypeScript, and no rebuild is needed. This must be served network-first with cache as offline fallback only, exactly like /books/*, and CACHE_NAME, STATIC_CACHE and SW_VERSION all bump together — the /books/* cache trap already cost one invisible content edit.

public/comfort/care.json — one row per campus id from CAMPUSES: the pastor's name, the destination email or form URL, and the response promise printed on the card. A campus pastor owns their own row. Today every campus in four countries shares one hardcoded mailto:care@futures.church.

public/comfort/lines.json — the crisis line per region: label, number, tel: href, hours sentence, plus the directory URL used when the region is unknown. Changing a number becomes a content edit rather than a deploy, which matters because these numbers do change.
public/comfort/flags.json — the crisis-language word list, per language, with an explicit false-positive exclusion list. Needs a named owner (see open decisions) but does not need a developer.
dw_comfort_daily — the reader's own lever, now in More instead of mid-flow, still synced through syncMisc.
The translation pills — the reader's lever, unchanged.

Honest exception: the comfort sectionOrder, the featured plan categories and the book-card ids stay in persona-config.ts and remain a developer edit. Everything a pastor would plausibly want to change in a hard week is in the four JSON files above; everything that changes the shape of the screen is code, and should be.

evidence.source: Ruling: feedback_daily_word_today_rebuild_rejected, 1 Sep 2026, line 11 — never merge a big IA/visual rebuild of the opening screen without Ashley previewing and approving it first.

open_decisions: The crisis lines per country. The research drafted US 988, AU 13 11 14, NZ 0800 543 354. Futures has 5 campuses in Indonesia and 1 in Brazil, and the research supplies no line for either — so an id or pt reader currently falls to 'unknown' and sees no number. Ashley picks the Indonesian and Brazilian lines, or rules that those regions show the local-emergency sentence plus the directory link only.

Who receives 'Talk to a pastor' at each campus, and what response promise we are allowed to print. One global care@futures.church, or a per-campus row in care.json. The copy says 'Someone from the church will read this and get back to you' — that is a promise with a name behind it, and it should not ship until the name exists.

Whether the comfort tap goes on every path's Home (one line under the reading) or lives only in More. It is the difference between comfort being available and comfort being findable, and it touches the opening screen for four of five paths — so it needs his preview either way.
Whether the return-day check-in ships at all. It is the only element in this design with no evidence behind it; the research explicitly marks it unsourced.
Who may edit flags.json, the crisis-language word list. It is content, but it decides when a card about self-harm appears on someone's screen.

Whether book cards may appear in comfort's done state at all, or whether comfort carries no promotion of any kind. The line is thin between 'when you're ready, there's more here' and selling a book to someone in crisis.

The 14 new anchor verses. Pairing verse to chapter takes the list from 16 to 30, so 14 pairings are Claude-drafted English content and need his sign-off before ship — he waived review on the comfort translations, not on new English.
Whether a person who uses the comfort tap three times in one week gets any human follow-up, and from whom.
risks: A false-positive safety card can read as surveillance — 'the app is watching what I type.' Mitigations: it never blocks, never sends, never stores the text (only that it fired), and one tap dismisses it for that conversation. If dismissal times cluster under two seconds, the word list is too loose and should be tightened, not expanded.

A missed true positive is the opposite failure and is far worse. The word list must be per-language, not machine-translated from English, and must be reviewed by someone who speaks the language — 'aku ingin mengakhiri semuanya' is not reachable from an English list.

Showing the wrong country's number is the specific industry failure the research names. The resolver must fail to 'no number' rather than to a US default, and comfort_line_shown's unknown rate must be watched from day one.

Moving comfort content into JSON walks straight into the /books/* service-worker trap: an edit that is invisible to every returning user. Network-first for /comfort/*, with CACHE_NAME, STATIC_CACHE and SW_VERSION bumped together in the same commit.

Removing the ask_lock step removes the only place dw_comfort_daily was ever set. If the inference does not fire, the value silently stays 0 and the tomorrow line never appears — which is why comfort_daily_inferred is on the event list.

The Comfort Home reshape is a big IA change to an opening screen, and the last one Ashley reverted the same night for being stripped. This one adds warmth and removes duplication rather than removing content, but it still ships behind a preview link and does not merge without his word.

Comfort Now opening as a full-screen host over Home is exactly the pattern that produced the two back-button findings. useSubView alone, mounted with a live open prop, and an Android back test in the preview before he looks at it.
Promising 'a person, not a bot' creates an operational obligation. If a campus does not answer, the app has lied to someone in crisis — which is a worse outcome than not having offered.

The comfort path will under-perform every other path on retention charts because it deliberately has no reminder, no streak and no graduation. If that gets read as failure in a dashboard review, the fix will be to add a nudge, which is the one thing this persona must never get.

Then npm run build and confirm the three SW constants changed in the built sw.js; reload a preview twice to prove an edited JSON appears without reinstalling the app.
